newsitem.title: UK: Britain announces one-year spending review.
newsitem.headline: Britain announces one-year spending review.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government is to launch a sweeping review of public spending that will set spending plans for the rest of this parliament, Chief Secretary to the Treasury Alistair Darling said on Wednesday.
The government will redirect spending to meet Labour's manifesto objectives while meeting existing targets, he told parliament.
"The government spends over 300 billion pounds ($491 billion) (each year)," Darling said. "We will reorder that 300 billion to meet our objectives..."
Darling, who as Chief Secretary holds the Treasury purse strings, said there was no better time for a "root and branch" reappraisal of public spending.
"We will...strip out ill-targeted spending programmes that benefit only the few, and redirect spending towards the priorities of the many," he said.

He said the review would take 12 months to complete, covering all government departments. "Its conclusions will inform a new set of public spending plans for the rest of this parliament. It will take the long-term view."
Each department must ask itself how its budget is spent, what is it achieving and how effective it is, Darling said.
"Every objective will be costed and departments' effectiveness in achieving them will be scrutinised."
The review will also determine what services should be provided by the public sector, the private sector or through a partnership.

"It will examine how we can achieve our objectives of improving standards in education, modernising the welfare state and getting people into work -- in short delivering our manifesto commitments as efficiently and effectively as we can," he said. ($ = 0.610 British Pounds)
